I founded it.

But I had worked for an agency in Connecticut, the only agency I ever worked for, actually, and just realized there was like, there was an opening for a bit of a fresh approach to the agency model that was a little more client friendly and less layered.
And so as you may have experienced with your company, you don't really know what direction your company might take.
You've got great intentions.
I thought we were going to do a lot of production services, which we did.
We did like 800 videos for 300 videos for Facebook and 200 videos for eBay.
We did a lot of that sort of outsourced white label production work.

Nobody really even knew what that was, including me.
So I did all nighters researching it and trying to understand what the opportunity was.
And I realized if it was visual messaging to consumers, you know, I could tap into the best people.
I had the best creative resources around.
And so that relationship started very, very small with just a few test projects and scopes and, you know, kind of beating us along.
But we really grew as the digital shelf world grew.
Right.
So, you know, before COVID hit, we were the AOR for Craft for their digital shelf content, and we have a fully dedicated team here.
The relationship with Craft is about 8 years old and just keeps getting deeper and Deeper where we're really fully embedded.

We do the strategy, we do the content creation, we deliver it, we do the SEO, the Geo, we work directly with their brands and that's really gotten us attention in this space for best in class content creators.
And as an agency we've used that to grow with other clients from Tyson to Pillsbury to Ferraro Jellybeans.
Everyone's so excited.
Ferrari is a new client and have a gigantic shipment of jelly beans coming our way literally any day now.
So the office cannot wait for the sugar rush.
So it's become, you know, it's really become something that we are recognized as best in class for.
And we have done over 100,000 assets in this space over the years.
We know what's happening on Amazon versus Walmart versus Target, how that changes every day.
We know how to optimize for organic cert, how that changes every day.
We do everything in house with people who are really well versed in 360 agency messaging.
So they're not just coming at it from like a technical side or data analytics side.
They understand that we're messaging to the consumers right here.
And we also have a fully built out content studio where we're able to do really efficient, nimble content creation on demand.
Video stills, what have you to help support that content.
Like as an example for the Jelly Bean, they don't have any assets.
We're going to be shooting all this fun stuff for them.
So we still have another division that does imagine content design.
We're actually doing this huge gala event.
All of the graphics and screens for the event and external of the event center in New York City that's happening tomorrow night actually and they do a lot of branding and packaging design.
They're people I've worked with my entire career, super talented.
It's nice for me to still have my hand in that kind of broadcast music world, which is really fun.
But you know, at its core our right to win category is really in the digital shelf right now.
And that's kind of a big overview.
Happy to answer any questions from there.
Perfect.
Yeah, I do have a bunch of questions, but I'll maybe give an intro on our side first.
So group 8A, I don't know if you've had a chance to look at our site.
I'm sure you have and look into us at all.
We're a performance digital marketing agency, very E commerce based, very direct to consumer based.
So we work with a lot of brands that have wholesale, that have B2B but we focus More on the direct to consumer side of the marketing.
We've been around for about 15 years.
We restructured a bit about 10 years ago so our current form is about 10 years old.
The main things we service in paid media is paid social, paid search, affiliate marketing, influencer marketing, email, sms.
We do have an in house design team, we do have an in house digital development team for tracking and, and other development work.
And that's pretty much us from a scope perspective.
In a nutshell.
We were also founded as a solution to a better type of agency.
I think one of the ways in which we're a little separate, if I understand correctly is we're probably a little bit more mid market, small market brands, small.
Seems like you're a little bit more enterprise which I think is one of the reasons we're attracted at the opportunity and also one of the reasons that we'll have questions.
Right.
So we're looking to grow.
Yeah, we're looking to grow.
Part of the direction we have is to grow more into enterprise.
So we are evaluating different opportunities in which we could do that.
We have a very sound infrastructure, we have a very capable scope of service but we've just done a really good job of building a mid market size company that we have serviced.

So in order to to grow we're kind of looking at this opportunity as one, you have a self sustaining autonomous business that could continue operationally and then one that can potentially be utilized as kind of a synergy to be a door opener into enterprise.
Take everything we already have and level up into an expanded type of, type of brand that we work with.
So that's why we're interested in the conversation.
And I do have questions.
Yeah, that's great, thank you.
For that context, you know it's interesting.
We, we didn't start small right in that space.
Like our first client in the digital shelf was freaking Craft Times.
Sometimes I have to remind myself we were just like this little under the radar company and we kind of burst out.
We have done work with smaller companies and we don't really have a minimum scope of engagement so much.

But for me part of the interest in exploring an opportunity potentially with you is, you know, where are those synergies that will allow the company to get to the next level and create a more diversified client base and more interesting work for the team and just kind of be able to capitalize on that.
Yeah.
So that that kind of segues into.
My first question is okay, to what extent do you have the capability to go like different size businesses?
We deal with startups, we deal with smaller brands that are looking to grow.
We deal with more mid size.
We deal with.
And so we're kind of across the board.
And I would say like our cap currently is like the low end of anything enterprise.
Right.
Like that's our cap right now.
But we're basically everything up until then.
So how much does the model fit it into?
Yes, we can work with a startup and we can curate it to service them versus hey, no, we just have our process and it works best yet.
No, it's 100%.
And in fact, you know, going back to like the different agency model, we're not crazy layered here.
We don't, you know, have, we're actually super competitively priced.
So we have all of those things that work at an enterprise level, but they also serve the smaller clients really well.
We just finished a project with a really small, small medical device brand.
You know, the kind of like wrist guards and stuff that you wear really small, just like seven deliverables.
On their scope of work, they're not enterprise level at all.
But our process for how we create the content remains the same.
Right.
So we don't have to compromise the quality in the way we work for a smaller client versus a bigger client.
It's just a matter of scale.
Okay, can you run me through from like basically the process like you're, you sign a new account or you start a conversation for a prospective client.
What is that process and how does the pricing work?
You mentioned you're competitively priced.
Just, just so I get a sense of the workflow and what the team looks like.
Yeah, sure.
So you know, it can run a few different ways.
We kind of adapt our model to what the client needs from us.
Right.
So we do have a retainer model with some clients where they're paying for the fully dedicated team or like 25% of a project manager or whatever.

But it's a retainer model where we know how many hours we're getting every month and those people are dedicated and we know roughly how long each kind of project will take so we can make sure that we can accomplish their deliverables.
We have other clients who are just per deliverable client.
So they need five product pages with mobile heroes and copy.
You know, we have sort of a price point for that based on, on what assets and things they might have.

So if a new client comes in the door, we'll have like a quick call with them and we'll try to understand what their goals are, what they don't like what they do like, about what content they may already have, what their internal process is, how many different parties have to weigh in and then really what assets they have.
It really comes down to like, do you have assets?
Are we making something up out of nothing?
Are we searching Shutterstock?
Are we searching, you know, trying to shoot something on the fly here?
Because obviously that adds hours and that will impact pricing.
But we do, we don't have a, a standard pricing.
But it's in my, for me, I have a framework for pricing and it's based a bit on scale.
If somebody's doing a brand new client, we'll charge them a minimal onboarding fee to get up to speed with their brand, their tone of voice or guidelines.
That could be as little as 5 or $10,000, depending on how, how many.
You know, sometimes a conglomerate will have multiple brands under them, right?
So it's a little more if we're trying to onboard with multiple brands versus just like one brand.
But it's really important to have that onboarding and just really get aligned with what they want to communicate about their product and what their workflow is like.
And then based on, you know, that initial we want to work with, you call, we figure out internally, like, okay, this is probably like a tier 2 project.
They don't have a lot of assets.
It's going to take a little more time.
We should probably go at the higher number, which is closer to maybe 3,000 per product page.
Right.
And like that's a package.
They get the copy, they get the mobile hero, they get the carousels for that.
And we know internally that we can hit 25 to 30% margin on that pricing based on what the assets they're going to give us are and how we approach at work, if that makes sense.
And then once, you know, once we have assigned scope of work, we get a brief from the client, we brief our teams internally.
We have project management, we have account management, we've got art directors, we've got copywriters.
We have also, in addition to our internal staff, we have an external team of people that we rely on as we need to flex or not.
So there's people who trained in how we work and what we do, which is, you know, takes time and effort.
So we try to have a group of four to five art directors, three or four copywriters that we, you know, can call.
If one's busy, we have another one.
We just have that sort of pool of people that we can seamlessly integrate.
And then, you know, if and when the workflow needs more people to come on staff.
We can tap into that.
We've sort of field our own staff training in that way.

I'm just curious.

Like, it's very hard to get that kind of granular sales data from any of those retailers.
So to the extent we can get it, we do, but it's not, it's not as database as you might imagine.
It's really more creative.
It's about messaging, it's about best in class principles.
It's about what we have learned over the years from different test and learn programs we were trying to be a part of.
There's a few companies out there that attempt to use like, heat mapping of an image to tell you if it's going to resonate or not.
And they always come back and say like, well, if you redesign the packaging and you didn't have green as your primary color, you know, it's like, well, they're not going to redesign their packaging.
So, you know, we haven't found any of those methods to actually be correct for us, you know, verifiable.
And we're always looking at them and we're always asked to vet them.
It's.
It's a very odd thing because if you say, like, well, what are your.
What's your measurement for success?
How do clients know if you've done a good job for them?

And you can't have this many characters here, but that many characters there.
And, you know, the number one thing these clients need is their products to show up on those digital shelves.

That's a huge business motivator right then and there.

We don't even have to ask any questions, like, we know what to do.

Got it.

It's me.

What is it?
If you knowing where the business has now, how would you scale it in your ideal world if you could plug and play with a sales funnel?
That's a really good question because I think it could take a, it could take two different tracks, right?
Sure.
It'd be great to have other enterprise level clients.
You know, the good and bad of that is it restricts you a little bit because you know, you get into non competes and you get stuck in.
Not every enterprise level client is necessarily a productive client and some of them have like crazy payment terms like 130 days and you know, so that it comes with some of its intricacies.
I think for the team creatively they would appreciate having more diversified clients to work on as opposed to just one other big.
So you know, if we're concentrating our time, bigger client, bigger payoff, right?
Bigger contract.
If you have 10 smaller clients, it's more work to service them and to, you know, ensure longevity.
If you have an enterprise level client, bigger contracts, it's, you know, more, more profitable presumably.
So if we were to concentrate our time, I think there's plenty of enterprise level contacts out there for the taking.
I see it in the industry, I see how it's evolving.
You also get more competition from the traditional agencies.

And I, and that's where I hesitate and think that sometimes the easier sell is for the one step under the enterprise level client because they're not worried about necessarily conflicting with like the fool says, gigantic global contract they have, you know, there's more opportunity.
And I also see, I mean I, you know, we have a couple clients in that tier and their departments are so overwhelmed.
There's two people not just managing the content but managing everything e commerce related and that's where we really excel.
Going in and partnering up and taking that load off and really being an extension of their internal team.
It's just, it's a numbers game.
Right.

And having a great balance of both will really ensure like kind of continuous success.
Yeah, because part of the reason I'm asking is I'm trying to figure out what we could actually do, right.

But mid market doesn't really work within your model.

It does work.
I think.

20 products to work on, right.

Right?

You know, it's something, it's really simple like do a good job and give a shit.
It's pretty rare.
Turns out it's pretty rare, right?
Like they all know they have direct contact to me and that I have eyes on everything.
And they all know my executive creative director has eyes on everything.
We're not farming this out to interns.
We're not sending this overseas where there might be other issues.

Like, no, you didn't give us 12 weeks notice.
We can't do this.

While they are getting end capel boards and being shouted out by, you know, Walmart as having great content and that kind of thing.

No partners, no investors, nothing like that.

So just to be clear, you're, you're, you're looking to stay on, just looking for a relationship that has that aligned partner, that synergy that fits or at some point are you looking to move on once?

I'm an entrepreneur.
I've come to realize I've been.

So I'll do what I need to do to make sure that happens.
But I don't think anything me is so special that, you know, somebody else can't do that.
It's just how where we're at right now.
Perfect.
I know we're.
We're at time.
I do have a stop.
Okay.
First of all, sounds like or seems like a really great brand.
It's why we.

Everything on this call kind of reinforced that.

Yeah, absolutely.
I would expect that you're going to want to have some more conversations, so I'm happy to.
Or shoot me a note if there's a quick question.
Whatever's helpful.
Amazing.
Ahmed, did we miss anything?
Are we good?
Yeah, I think that's pretty much good for the first call.
And yeah, thank you so much for joining the call guys.
And I'll follow up with everyone for the next steps.
And Ari, we'll be in touch.
Great to meet you, Ari.
Thank you so much.
Great to meet you, too.
Thanks, everyone.
Thank you.
Thanks.
Bye.
Bye.
Ahmed, do you want to connect?
Sure.
I don't know if it's their note taker.
Just remove that.

summary.overview:
- **Company Expertise:** Imaginary Content has created over 100,000 digital assets, specializing in e-commerce content for major brands.  
- **Diverse Client Base:** They successfully serve both enterprise and smaller clients, balancing quality with scalable content production.  
- **Flexible Service Model:** Pricing for projects averages $3,000, with onboarding fees between $5,000-$10,000, ensuring tailored client engagement.  
- **Sales Challenges:** Lack of a scalable sales funnel hinders growth; strategies needed to generate consistent qualified leads beyond referrals.  
- **Retention Strategy:** High-quality service and immediate executive involvement drive strong client loyalty compared to larger agencies.  
- **Growth Partnership:** Seeking a partner to enhance sales capacity while preserving company culture and service quality for sustainable success.
summary.short_summary: Imaginary Content, a digital shelf content agency founded by Ilene Richardson, has delivered over 100,000 assets, maintaining strong partnerships with brands like Craft and Tyson. The agency balances serving both enterprise and smaller clients, with a flexible pricing model averaging $3,000 per project and onboarding fees between $5,000-$10,000. Despite its success, the company faces sales growth challenges, primarily due to a lack of a scalable sales funnel, relying heavily on word-of-mouth referrals. Ilene aims to find a strategic partner to enhance sales capacity while preserving the company's culture and quality standards. The agency's exceptional client retention is driven by high-quality service and executive oversight, a key differentiator in the competitive e-commerce landscape.
